Yes, a third trimester ultrasound can predict the presentation of the first twin at delivery with a high degree of accuracy, but it's not 100% reliable. The presentation of the first twin refers to the position of the baby in the womb, such as head-down, breech, or transverse. 

Studies have shown that an ultrasound performed after 32 weeks of gestation can accurately predict the presentation of the first twin in about 80-90% of cases. However, the accuracy may decrease as the gestational age approaches term, due to the increased mobility of the twins and potential changes in their positions.

It's essential to note that while third trimester ultrasound can provide valuable information, it's just one tool used to assess the presentation of the first twin. Other factors, such as the overall health of the mother and the twins, as well as the presence of any complications, will also be taken into account when determining the best course of care for delivery.
